sections.title: What the theorem establishes
sections.text: The element-trace series of the Frenkel–Lepowsky–Meurman Monster module are genus-zero Hauptmoduls, proving the main Conway–Norton moonshine conjecture.

sections.title: Proof architecture
sections.text: The vertex algebra and no-ghost theorem produce the Monster Lie algebra. Its twisted denominator identities constrain trace coefficients. Section 9 compares these recurrences with those of the proposed modular functions.

sections.title: Why finite checking suffices here
sections.text: Recurrences propagate appropriate initial character information, including information for powers of group elements, to all coefficients. The paper does not infer an infinite identity merely from several matching numerical terms.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.text: Character decompositions determine the needed initial values; recursion then identifies the entire series. This is a proof conditional on the established constructions and earlier results, not a statistical experiment.

sections.title: Reading boundary
sections.text: This guide explains the introduction and final comparison. It does not reproduce the no-ghost argument or verify every intermediate algebraic construction.
